verified.bloom_gates: G1 yes (FDA/CBER is a named counterparty with a dated action). G2 yes (the PDUFA goal date is a concrete regulatory commitment). G3 partial: the binary is open, but its value is probability-weighted and the negative AdCom has already been priced in, so it is not a clearly unpriced figure.
verified.edge: L-M. Run-up from the pre-catalyst base: about 0-5%. The stock has sat around $7.6-8.0 since the 9-03 AdCom washout (50d avg $7.64, spot $7.83), so it has not run up. Remaining to the favorable value: about +90-130% if approved (my own rough estimate of ~$15-18/sh: approved rare-disease DMD asset, narrow upper-limb label, US partner economics). Floor if rejected: about $3.5-4/sh in net cash, roughly -50 to -55%. With approval odds of maybe 30-35% after the negative AdCom, the probability-weighted value is about $7-8, close to spot. The asymmetry is real but about fairly priced. There is no clear mispricing edge.
verified.primary_source: Capricor press release, GlobeNewswire 2026-10-05 ('Positive HOPE-3 OLE Data on Upper Limb Function... PDUFA Target Action Date November 22, 2026'). Capricor 10-Q for Q2 2026, filed 2026-08-14 (FMP balance sheet). FMP quote 2026-10-12 ($7.83, mcap $450M). Hagens Berman notice 2026-09-27 (FDA extended the BLA review).
verified.analysis: Capricor's own 2026-10-05 press release confirms the PDUFA date of 2026-11-22 and says the upper-limb HOPE-3 OLE data went into a BLA major amendment. That means the date is company-confirmed, not single-source as triage said. The upper-limb-only label is implied by how the amendment is framed but not stated outright. The capital structure is clean: per the 6/30/26 10-Q there is no preferred and no funded debt, ~$238M of cash and investments against ~$91M of lease liabilities, and ~58M shares. That gives a cash floor of about $3.5-4/sh after burn, so the equity waterfall does not cap the event. The binary is still forward and unharvested. But after a negative AdCom and with the securities class action about a rewritten SAP outstanding, approval odds are low enough that spot roughly equals the expected value. Gaps: web search budget was exhausted, so I did not independently verify the AdCom vote details, the reported $2 PT, or the partner milestone terms.

verified.instrument: CBRS common (NASDAQ). Reference $164.17 on 2026-10-12, just above the 52-week low of $160.81 and under the $185 IPO price.
verified.bloom_gates: None passed. G1: no named counterparty, because a lockup expiry is a supply event, not a deal with someone. G2: no concrete company commitment. G3: no specific figure that the market has not priced; the expiry date and share count are public in the S-1/424B4. The OpenAI 750MW / $25.4B RPO backlog is already known and is not this catalyst.
verified.edge: L. Lockup dates are among the most widely known calendar events, and the staged early release (about Oct 1) has already been sold into. Insider Form 4 sales on Sep 28-29 were COO 396k shares at about $204 and CFO 32.5k shares. CNBC on 2026-10-02 put the -20% week down to the lockup plus the loss of OpenAI's Ultrafast workload to Nvidia. Run-up from the pre-catalyst base: none. The stock fell about 20%, from about $204 on Sep 29 to $164, so the overhang discount has already been taken. Remaining capture to the favorable value (back to the $185 IPO price after the overhang clears): about +13%. That figure is not provenance-checked, because the payoff depends on sentiment and OpenAI concentration, not on the capital structure. Much of the overhang may already be priced, and the November release can still add supply first.
verified.primary_source: SEC EDGAR: CBRS 424B4 filed 2026-05-14 (cerebras-424b4.htm; IPO priced 2026-05-13) and the closing 8-K filed 2026-05-15. CNBC 2026-10-02, "Cerebras stock hits post-IPO low...lockup expiration". Form 4 sales dated 2026-09-28/29, via Defense World 2026-10-01. FMP quote 2026-10-12 ($164.17, 52-week range $160.81-$386.34).
verified.analysis: The event is real, dated (about Nov 9-10) and still ahead, but it is a technical supply event with no Bloom gate. The early release has already happened and the stock already fell about 20% around it, so the clean overhang-clearing setup is mostly used up. What the stock does next depends on OpenAI concentration (it lost the Ultrafast workload to Nvidia, then Altman called Cerebras a "close partner" on Oct 5) and on the Q3 guide, not on the lockup itself. Gaps: web search was exhausted this turn, so I could not read the lock-up clause in the 424B4 for the exact date, any earnings-linked early-release triggers, or the number of shares unlocking. The date is inferred as 180 days after the 2026-05-13 pricing. I also skipped the numerator-provenance check, since the upside does not come from the capital structure. Score 3, no tier: watch it only as a timing tool after the expiry, not as a catalyst.
